correctness.rationale: For each cubic F, geometric smoothness is equivalent to rank 56 of S_3^4 to S_5 multiplication by its four partial derivatives (regular sequence socle-degree argument). Complete orbit enumeration covers all 2^20-1 nonzero forms, identifies 36 smooth orbits and 322560 forms; all 36 reps pass independent unit Groebner ideals on all four affine charts. The ordered-basis histogram is exhaustively weighted by orbit size and divided by 6, with independent Walsh transform confirming 30017433600 ordered triples and separate Python evaluation reproducing every base-point bin. The 56 fifteen-base pencils, single orbit, and five skew shared rational lines have a third direct exhaustive checker. Rational 14-base impossibility has a separate parity proof.

originality.rationale: The closest published works provide the existence framework for all-smooth finite-field pencils, and exact classification of individual binary cubic surfaces, but not the additive triple compatibility count, its complete rational-base distribution, or the 56-pencil maximal incidence orbit. Direct mathematical implications were checked: knowing the 36 individual surface orbits or the 28 smooth point-filling surfaces alone does not determine the pairwise condition F+G smooth. An unindexed computed census is a remaining priority risk.
residual_risks: Historical small-field enumerations or datasets not indexed in the consulted literature could explicitly contain the binary cubic-surface pencil histogram.

Karaoglu publishes full cubic surface orbit representatives, so some pencil counts could in principle be postprocessed from those known data; new value rests on the separate additive incidence enumeration and extremal geometry.

value.rationale: It classifies a natural finite-field smooth-linear-system incidence space, not merely individual cubic surfaces: 5,002,905,600 smooth pencils with all possible rational base cardinalities, a structural forbidden 14-point stratum, and one 56-element extremal orbit whose five mutually skew common lines partition the ambient rational projective points. These are motivated refinements of small-field pencil existence and finite cubic-surface arithmetic.
